verdicts.rationale: Both are Wittgenstein's 'Philosophical Investigations', 1953. Different publishers (Macmillan/Blackwell) reflect US vs UK issue of the same work.
Both are Wittgenstein's 'Philosophical Investigations', 1953; same work despite publisher variance (Macmillan vs Blackwell).
Both 'Tractatus Logico-Philosophicus', Wittgenstein, 1961, Routledge & Kegan Paul. Same work.
Both 'Art and Its Objects', Wollheim, 1980, Cambridge University Press. 2nd ed. vs base title, same work.
'Art and its Objects, 2nd ed' and 'Art and its Objects: With Six Supplementary Essays', both 1980. The 2nd edition added the six supplementary essays; same work/edition.
'Art and Its Objects' and 'Art and its Objects: With Six Supplementary Essays', both Wollheim 1980. Same work.

'Sketch-a-net that beats humans' (2015 arXiv 1501.07873) and 'Sketch-a-Net: A Deep Neural Network that Beats Humans' (2017 IJCV). Preprint and published version of the same paper by overlapping author team.

Both 'Vision as Bayesian inference: analysis by synthesis?', Trends in Cognitive Sciences 10(7):301-308, 2006. a's malformed title embeds the same venue/vol/pages; author list matches (Yuille & Kersten).

Two distinct consecutive papers in Neuroscience 9(4) 1983: 'The reaction of cells...to wavelengths and colours' (pp. 741-765, doi ...90265-8) vs 'The responses of wavelength-selective and colour-coded cells...' (pp. 767-781, doi ...90266-x). Different subtitles, pages, and DOIs.
Both 'Beyond ‘What’ and ‘How Many’...', Zosh & Feigenson, 2009, Oxford University Press, in 'The Origins of Object Knowledge', pp. 25-51/25-52. Same chapter.
